newKindNeeds.summary: Lock a known multiple for H months versus rolling a short-term rate every p months for the same H months, replayed from every start month in history. One spec serves retire-4 (savings bond doubling vs 3-month T-bills, H=240, p=1) and retire-3 (5-year yield locked vs 1-year yield rolled, H=60, p=12).

inputs.roll: monthly CSV (date column YYYY-MM-01, value column = annual rate in percent): the rate earned by each roll period. Params: file, dateColumn, valueColumn, periodMonths p (1 = monthly roll of a 3-month bill as in retire-4; 12 = yearly roll of a 1-year yield as in retire-3). H must be a multiple of p.
inputs.lock: EITHER a constant multiple m reached at H months (retire-4: m = 2.0, the savings bond guarantee) OR a monthly CSV of the locked annual rate L with its own periodMonths q (retire-3: GS5, q = 12).
inputs.optional: firstStart / lastStart (months; default = every month whose inputs all exist); subsets {name: [from, to|null]} of start months (may overlap); startFilter {type: 'rollRateAboveLockRate'} (retire-3: GS1(s) > GS5(s)) with runs of consecutive filtered months; deflator CSV (CPI) for buying power; nearBandPct; conventions; notModel.
inputs.dates: months written YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-01 compare equal after normalising (lessons from K3.5/K3.6).

newKindNeeds.calculation: For each start month s with all inputs present: Roll(s) = product over k = 0 .. H/p − 1 of (1 + R(s + k·p) · p/1200); Lock(s) = m if constant, else (1 + L(s) · q/1200)^(H/q). A window is 'roll ahead' if Roll > Lock and 'lock ahead' if Lock > Roll (strict; ties in neither). With a deflator P: real value of each leg = leg × P(s)/P(s + H); windows where P is missing at either end are skipped and counted. Shares are 100 × count / windows in the set (all, each subset, the filtered starts). Runs = maximal sequences of consecutive calendar months inside the filtered starts; a run is 'lock-majority' if more than half its starts are lock ahead.
newKindNeeds.outputs: echo of params; nWindows, firstStart, lastStart; shareRollAhead, shareLockAhead; median/min/max of Roll and of Lock/Roll − 1 (in %), with the start month of min and max (ties: earliest); latest window {start, end, roll, lock}; equivalentLockRate = 100(m^(12/H) − 1) for a constant lock; per subset {from, to, nWindows, shareRollAhead, shareLockAhead, minRoll, maxRoll}; filtered set {nWindows, shareLockAhead, median/min/max Lock/Roll − 1, runs, lockMajorityRuns}; deflator {nRealWindows, skippedStarts, shareLockRealAtLeastOne, medianLockReal, minLockReal + start, lastStartLockRealBelowOne}; nearCount; rollRateLatest {month, value}; windows: [{start, end, roll, lock, real?}] for every window. Values unrounded in the model file.
invariants: Constant rate check: replacing R by a constant r gives Roll = (1 + r·p/1200)^(H/p) in every window (±1e-12 relative).
With p = 1, Roll(s) equals G(s+H)/G(s) for the running index G (cumulative product), i.e. the product and index methods agree.
shareRollAhead + shareLockAhead + shareTie = 100 for every set; nWindows of the subsets that partition the range add up to nWindows.
Each window uses exactly H/p roll observations and ends at s + H − 1 ≤ the last data month.
Raising every roll rate by δ > 0 never lowers shareRollAhead (monotonic).
Constant lock m = 2, H = 240 → equivalentLockRate = 3.526 % a year; real value = m × P(s)/P(s+H).

retire3Instance.note: retire-3's lock leg compounds once a year at GS5(s); its 'lock ahead' share (65.2% all, 64.4% inverted) is shareLockAhead. Checked against retire-3/result.json by episodes/ep003/model/model.py --retire3 (ledger ep003).
